evidence.estrutura: Barrios organized through miners' communities, unions and housewives' committees, emphasizing worker and community organization from below rather than centralized elite rule. This supports participatory collective organization more than territorial federalism.
evidence.representacao: She organized women and miners politically, ran for office and used testimony to demand that poor working-class communities be heard. This strongly supports mass political participation and representation of excluded groups.
evidence.poder: Her activism confronted military dictatorships, imprisonment and massacres, strongly supporting resistance to authoritarian coercion and arbitrary state violence.
evidence.imigracao: Her political work centered Bolivian miners and class struggle rather than immigration policy. No reliable border doctrine is established.
evidence.diplomacia: Her participation in the 1975 International Women's Year conference and transnational testimony show international advocacy, but not a detailed state diplomacy doctrine.
evidence.intervencao: Her struggle against military dictatorship and repression was primarily organized through strikes, testimony and mass mobilization rather than foreign military intervention. This supports anti-militarist restraint.
evidence.economia: Her testimony explicitly analyzes class exploitation, mine workers' poverty and enrichment of owners, supporting a strongly socialist or worker-oriented economic position.
evidence.controle: She supported unions, collective struggle and social control over economic conditions, implying substantial coordination and regulation beyond laissez-faire markets.
evidence.comercio: Her critique targets capitalist exploitation rather than international trade as such. No clean free-trade versus protectionist doctrine is established; use a moderately anti-laissez-faire placement.
evidence.religiao: Her political arguments were centered on class and democracy rather than religious authority. No case exists for clerical government.
evidence.moral: Her organizing elevated working-class women as political actors and challenged both class and gender subordination, supporting progressive egalitarian social values.
evidence.tecnologia: Her work arose in mining communities and focused on labor conditions rather than technology policy. Use a moderate position.
